div.label: a. Take Heed of an Idle and Slothful Spirit
div.p:
FirſtFirst, Asas ever you would give up your ſelvesselvesyourselves to private prayer, Taketake heed of an idle and ſloathfulslothfulsloathful ſpiritspirit. If Adam in the ſtatestate of Innocencyinnocence muſtmust work and dreſsdress the Gardengarden;, and if after his fall,Fall when he was Monarchmonarch of all the world, he muſtmust yet labourlabor, why ſhouldshould any be idle or ſloathfulslothfulsloathful? IdleneſsIdleness is a ſinsin againſtagainst the law of Creationcreation:. God creating man to labourlabor, the idle perſonperson violates this Lawlaw of Creationcreation,; for by his idleneſsidleness he caſtscasts off the authority of his Creator, who Who made him for labourlabor. IdleneſsIdleness is a contradiction to the AuguſtAugust. de Gen ad. lit. lib. 8. cap. 8. principles of our Creationcreation. Man in Innocencyinnocence ſhouldshould have been freed from wearineſsweariness, but not from employment; he was to dreſsdress the Gardengarden by divine appoyntment;appointment. “
And the Lord God took the man, and put Gen. 2. 15. him into the Gardengarden of Eden, to dreſsdress it, and to keep itit” (Gen 2:15). All wearineſsweariness in labourlabor, and all vexing, tyringtiring, and tormenting labourlabor, came in by the fall,Fall. “ In the ſweatsweat of thy face ſhaltshalt thou eat Gen. 3. 19. breadbread” (Gen 3:19). The bread of idleneſsidleness is neither ſweetsweet nor ſuresure.. “ An idle perſonsoulperson ſhallshall ſuffersuffer Pro. 19. 15. hunger,,” ſaithsaith SolomonSolomon (Pro 19:15). An idle life, & and an holy heart are far enough aſunderasunder.. “ By doing nothing (,” ſaithsaith the Heathenheathen man), “ men learn to do evil things:.” It is eaſieeasy ſlippingslipping out of an idle life into an evil and wicked life;. yeaYea, an idle life is of it ſelfselfitself evil;, for man was made to be active, not to be idle. The CyclopesCyclops thought mansman’s happineſshappiness did conſiſtconsist in nihil agendo, in doing nothing:, Butbut no excellent thing 1 Cor. 1. 17. Eph. 4. 28. 2 TheſThes. 3. 10, 12. can be the child of idleneſsidleness. IdleneſsIdleness is a mothermother- ſinsin, a breedingbreeding- ſinsin, 'tis. It is pulvinar diaboli, the devilsdevil’s cuſhioncushion,cushion on which he ſitssits;, &and the devilsdevil’s anvileanvil, on which he frames very great, and very many ſinssins (Eph 4:28; 2Th 3:10, 12)sins. LookLook, as Toadstoads and Serpentsserpents breed moſtmost in ſtandingstanding waters, ſoso ſinsin thrives moſtmost in
idle perſonspersons. IdleneſsIdleness is that which provokes the Lord to forſakeforsake mensmen’s bodies, and the Devildevil to poſſeſspossess their ſoulssouls.

No man hath leſsless means to preſervepreserve his body, and more temptations to infect his ſoulsoul, than an idle perſonperson. OOh, ſhakeshake off ſlothsloth.! The ſluggiſhsluggish ChriſtianChristian will be ſleepingsleeping,sleeping or idling, or trifling, when he ſhouldshould be in his cloſetcloset aa- praying. Sloth is the Greengreen-ſickneſssickness of the ſoulsoul; get it cured, or 'twillit will be your eternal bane. Of all Devilsdevils, 'tisit is the idle Devildevil that keeps men moſtmost out of their CloſetsclosetsClosets. There is nothing that gives the devil ſoso much advantage againſtagainst us as idleneſsidleness. 'TwasIt was'twas Hierom. ep. 4. good counſelcounsel that JeromJerome gave to his friend, Facito aliquid operis, ut te ſempersemper Diabolus inveniat occupatum,, “Do some work so that the devil always finds you busy,” that when the Devildevil comes with a temptation, you may anſweranswer him, you are not at leaſureleisureleasure.

It was the ſpeechspeech of Mr. Greenham (ſometimessometimes, a famous &and painful preacher of this nation), that when the Devildevil tempted a poor ſoulsoul, ſheshe
came to him for advice, how ſheshe might reſiſtresist the temptation, and he gave her this anſweranswer,: “ Never be idle, but be alwayesalways well employed,. forFor in my own experienceexperience, I have found it;, when the Devildevil came to tempt me, I told him that I was not at leaſureleisureleasure to hearken to his temptations,; and by this means I reſiſtedresisted all his aſſaultsassaults..” IdleneſsIdleness is the hour of temptation,; and an idle perſonperson is the Devilsdevil’s Tennistennis-Ballball, toſſedtossed by him at his pleaſurepleasure.

He“He that labourslabors,” (ſaidsaid the old Hermite)hermit, “ is tempted but by one Devildevil, but he that is idle is aſſaultedassaulted by all..” Cupid complained, that he could never faſtenfasten upon the MuſesMuses, becauſebecause he could never find them idle. The Fowlerfowler bends his bow and ſpreadsspreads his net for Birdsbirds when they are ſetset, not when they are upon the wing:. So Satan ſhootsshoots his moſtmost fiery darts at men, when they are moſtmost idle and ſloathfulslothfulsloathful:. And this the Sodomites found by wofulwoeful experienceexperience (Eze 16:49), when God rained Ezek. 16. 49. hell out of heaven upon them,
both for their idleneſsidleness, and for thoſethose other ſinssins of theirs, which their idleneſsidleness did expoſeexpose them to.

It was ſaidsaid of Rome, that during the time of their wars with Carthage and other enemies in Africa, they knew not what vice meant; but no ſoonersooner had they got the conqueſtconquest, but through idleneſsidleness they came to ruineruin. IdleneſsIdleness is a ſinsin, not only againſtagainst the Lawlaw of Gracegrace, but alſoalso againſtagainst the light of nature. You cannot look any wayway, but every creature checks and upbraids your idleneſsidleness and ſlothsloth;. ifIf you look up to the heavens, there you ſhallshall find all their glorious Lightslights conſtantconstant in their motions:. PſalPsal. 104. 23. blow, the Waterswaters run, the Earthearth brings forth her pleaſantpleasant and delightful fruits,. allAll the FiſhfishFish in the Seasea, Fowlsfowls in the Airair, and BeaſtsbeastsBeasts in the Fields,fields and on the Mountains,mountains have their motions and operations, all which call aloud upon
man not to be idle, but active.

And let me ſendsend you to the buſiebusy BeeBe,bee to learn activity and induſtryindustry;. thoughThough the BeebeeBe be little in bulk, yet 'tisit is great in ſerviceservice;. ſheSheshe flyesflies far, examines the fields, hedges, trees, orchards, gardens, and loads her ſelfselfherself with honey and wax, and then returns to her Hivehive.

Now how ſhouldshould the activity of theſethese creatures put the idle perſonperson to a bluſhblush. O Sirssirs,! Man is thatthe moſtmost noble creature, into whom God hath
put principles of the greateſtgreatest activity, as capable of the greateſtgreatest and higheſthighest enjoyments; and thereforetherefore, idleneſsidleness is a forgetting mansman’s dignity, and a forſakingforsaking of that rank that God hath ſetset him in, and a debaſingdebasing of himſelfhimself below the leaſtleast and meaneſtmeanest creatures, who conſtantlyconstantly in their order obedientiallyobediently ſerveserve the Lawlaw of their creation. Nay, if you look up to the bleſſedblessed Angelsangels above you, you ſhallshall ſtillstill find them active and ſerviceableserviceable;. “ Are they not all miniſtringministering Spiritsspirits, ſentsent Heb. 1. 14. forth to miniſterminister for them, who ſhallshall be heirs of ſalvationsalvation??” (Heb 1:14). And if you look down to the Angelsangels of darkneſsdarkness below you, Ooh, how laborious and induſtriousindustrious are they, to deſtroydestroy and 1 Pet. 5. 8. damnedamn your precious and immortal ſoulssouls (1Pe 5:8)souls!

For a cloſeclose,close remember, that idleneſsidleness is ſoso great an evil, that it hath been condemned and ſeverelyseverely puniſhedpunished by the very worſtworst of men. Among the Egyptians, IdleneſsidlenessIdleness was a capital crime. Among the Lucans, he that lent money to an
